subject: Reserved commit term options / flexible start date - HorizonCloud
message_1_subject: Question on commit term & flexible start
message_1_body:
Hi Dev,

Thanks for the demo last week — the dedicated offering looks promising. Procurement asked for a clearer breakdown of the 12/24/36-month reserved commit options: specifically how discount tiers change with committed GPU-pool size, whether we can push the official capacity start date (we'd like a 30–60 day buffer before the billing start), and what guarantees you provide for baseline throughput during ramp.

We have an internal timeline that favors a September production start, but procurement wants contract alignment earlier. Can you send scenarios showing: (A) aggressive ramp (full pool by month 3), (B) phased ramp (50% month 1, 75% month 2, 100% month 4), and (C) a delayed billing start with a 60-day free prep window? If you have a one-pager on billing milestones and credits for missed SLOs, that would help.

Appreciate it — copying procurement.

Thanks,
Sarah Li
Director, Cloud Platform
HorizonCloud

message_2_subject: Re: Question on commit term & flexible start
message_2_body:
Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and for looping procurement. Quick summary below and I attached a spreadsheet with line-item scenarios (RC_Term_Scenarios_v3.xlsx).

Short answers:
- Discounts scale with committed monthly GPU-hours; roughly 8%/13%/18% for small/medium/large pools on 12m, add ~2–3ppt for 24m and ~4–6ppt for 36m depending on pool size.
- We can delay billing start up to 60 days with an agreed prep window, but pricing tiers are set on the signed committed quantity (we invoice from billing start).
- Throughput guarantees: baseline throughput SLA for the committed pool (tokens/sec and p99 latency) with automatic route-to-fallback on cold starts. Credits apply for monthly SLA miss >5%.

I've sketched three scenarios in the workbook per your A/B/C; highlights:
- Scenario A (aggressive): highest effective discount because you commit to bigger pool sooner; assumes 3-month onboarding professional services (billed) and full capacity by month 3.
- Scenario B (phased): modestly lower up-front discount; we recommend a 4-week canary for model variants to protect quality.
- Scenario C (delayed billing start): we can provide a 30–60 day prep window where we reserve capacity but do not invoice. The pool size is reserved at contract signing and billing starts on the agreed date.

Action items:
1) Confirm which scenario you want modeled at 3 pool sizes (Base/Plus/Peak) and I'll return a pro-forma with monthly milestones.
2) If procurement wants legal-level language on the start/date hold, I can loop Lauren for SOW/redline guardrails.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Head of Sales, Dedicated Products
Redwood Inference

message_3_subject: Re: Question on commit term & flexible start
message_3_body:
Hi Sarah — looping in a few legal/ops clarifications you may see in the SOW: 

1) Billing start vs. service start: We can formalize a "prep window" of up to 60 days where engineering work (onboarding, network setup, dry runs) occurs without charging reserved commit fees, but any professional services (e.g., migration assistance) will be billed separately if consumed.

2) Capacity guarantees: the contract will include a minimum throughput metric tied to the committed GPUPOOL (e.g., X tokens/sec per GPU aggregate) and a credit ladder (5% credits for SLA miss between 5–15%, 10% credits >15%). We avoid hard caps on burst capacity but can commit reasonable burst headroom in the SOW.

3) Ramp exceptions: If you request a delayed start after signing, we will maintain reserved capacity commitments for the signed term; pricing and discounts are based on the committed pool size at signing. If you materially change pool sizing before billing start, we can requote but may need an amendment.

Happy to provide draft SOW language.

—Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
message_4_subject: Re: Question on commit term & flexible start
message_4_body:
Sarah — adding a commercial option we've used with similar customers that may fit HorizonCloud's posture: a staged commitment with an initial 12-month contract that includes a 12-month extension option exercisable at month 9 (price locks for the extension). Benefits: you get faster procurement approval (lower initial commit) and optionality to extend at pre-agreed discounts.

Example outline:
- Initial commit: 12 months at Medium pool (with 12-month discount levels applied).
- Option: extend 12 or 24 months at a pre-set price band if exercised by month 9 of initial term.
- Prep window: 45 days free prep; billing starts on the agreed date or upon production cutover.

If HorizonCloud prefers long-term cost certainty, we can price a straight 36-month with highest discount; if procurement needs lower near-term cash out, the staged-commit + option hybrid often helps.

I'll prepare a one-page comparison table if you want to share with stakeholders.

-Rishi
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference
message_5_subject: Re: Question on commit term & flexible start
message_5_body:
Dev / Rishi / Lauren — thanks all, this is helpful. Procurement likes the staged-commit + option model as it keeps near-term OPEX lower while preserving a path to deeper discounts. A few clarifying items from procurement: 

- Can the prep window be 60 days for this deal and include a limited number of load tests (we'll provide scripts)?
- For the option exercise, can you guarantee the extension pricing band won't move beyond +/-2% relative to initial pricing if exercised at month 9? Procurement needs predictable budgeting.
- We're leaning to Medium pool initially but want a clear change-order path to add 25% capacity during month 6 with pro-rated billing.

If you can confirm those three items, procurement will prepare a redline-ready PO and we can move to DocuSign.

Best,
Sarah

message_6_subject: Re: Question on commit term & flexible start — confirmations and next steps
message_6_body:
Sarah — great, glad the hybrid model resonates. Confirming all three items: 

1) Prep window: we can commit to a 60-day prep window for this deal and include up to two full load-test runs (you provide scripts and test accounts). Any additional professional services/time will be scoped separately.

2) Extension pricing band: we'll lock the extension pricing at +/-2% of the initial unit price if exercised by month 9 — that will be called out in the amendment language.

3) Mid-term scale: change-orders to add +25% capacity at month 6 are supported; billing will be pro-rated from the effective change date and the added capacity will pick up the same unit discount band as the initial pool unless you elect to re-evaluate pool tiering (we'll provide a pro-forma for that).

Next steps: I will send an updated spreadsheet reflecting the staged-commit + option numbers and ask Lauren to add the SOW clause language for the 60-day prep window and pricing lock. If procurement is ready, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet (term sheet + SOW + amendment for the option) for signatures.

Target timeline: initial DocuSign sent by 2026-08-05, preferred production cutover window Sept 15–30.

Action: procurement to confirm they want DocuSign and provide PO metadata (PO number, billing contact).

Thanks — talk soon.
